fields.what_it_is: The Miethke Shunt System SHUNTASSISTANT (SA 2.0) is used for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunting. It is a valve with gravitational technology. Depending on the body position of the patient, the SHUNTASSISTANT 2.0 valve gradually adapts the opening pressure automatically and counteracts possible overdrainage. It can be combined with differential pressure valves (fixed or adjustable). The slim, cylindric design enables a fast and easy implantation and is suitable for adults as well as pediatric hydrocephalus treatment. SHUNTASSISTANT® 2.0 is also suitable for lumbar drainage due to two special variants. The functionality of the SHUNTASSISTANT 2.0 valve in different body positions is demonstrated in the MIETHKE® App. In the horizontal position, the SHUNTASSISTANT® 2.0 valve is always open and does not present any resistance. The opening pressure is exclusively determined by an additional differential pressure valve in this body position. When the patient moves into an upright position, the SHUNTASSISTANT 2.0 valve is activated by the tantalum ball (green) and adapts the valve opening pressure automatically.

fields.indications: The Miethke Shunt System SHUNTASSISTANT (SA 2.0) is used for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunting.
fields.compatible_with: It can be combined with differential pressure valves (fixed or adjustable).
fields.use_notes: As overdrainage protection, it can be combined with differential pressure valves (fixed or adjustable), either as an initial solution or as a secondary add-on device for patients with existing complications. The slim, cylindric design enables a fast and easy implantation. An implantation parallel to the body axis of the patient helps ensure a precise and reliable performance of the SHUNTASSISTANT 2.0 valve. The choice of the appropriate pressure level of the SHUNTASSISTANT® 2.0 valve depends on several other factors, including age, degree of activity, size and height of the patient. The values given apply to mobile patients. For patients with little mobility or a high BMI, a lower pressure level should be chosen for the gravitational unit.
